cards.explanation: The answer is True. Jesus says, "Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted." I think this one lands softly on a lot of hearts. Notice He doesn't say the mourning isn't real. He says comfort is coming for those who mourn.

The pattern is who is blessed and what they'll get. The poor in spirit get the kingdom of heaven, and those who mourn will be comforted. Each line names a group and then gives them a promise. It works like a label on a cookie box, friends: who it's for, then what's inside.

The word is filled. "Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled." Jesus promises that they will be filled. That's His word to people who hunger and thirst for what's right. I wish every batch I pulled out of the oven came with a promise like that.

The answer is False. There's a promise attached. Jesus says, "Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy." Every one of these blessings comes with something in return. This one is mercy for the merciful.
The word is pure. "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God." Jesus is talking about the heart, not the outside. And the promise is about as big as promises get: they will see God.

The answer is the peacemakers. "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God." That's a big name to be handed, friends. Jesus gives it to the people who make peace. They're the group He names.

The answer is righteousness. "Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness…" Jesus says they're persecuted for doing right, not for doing wrong. And He still calls them blessed. That's the kind of suffering He's talking about.

The answer is True. To the poor in spirit, Jesus says, "…theirs is the kingdom of heaven." To those persecuted because of righteousness, He says the very same words (Matthew 5:10). He starts and ends this stretch with the same promise, friends.

The answer is to rejoice and be glad. Jesus says, "Rejoice and be glad…" He tells them to be glad even while they're being insulted and persecuted because of Him. And He gives them something to hold onto: "…great is your reward in heaven…"

The answer is heaven. "Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven…" The reward is great, and Jesus puts it in heaven. He says this to people who are insulted and persecuted because of Him. He gives them that to rejoice about.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "…for in the same way they persecuted the prophets before you." So if His listeners are persecuted, they're in good company. The prophets went through the same thing before them.

The answer is that it's thrown out and trampled. Salt that loses its savor is "…no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled by men." Jesus asks how it could be made salty again. He gives no answer, just where it ends up.
The answer is False. There are no loopholes here, friends. Jesus says, "A city on a hill cannot be hidden." It's a plain statement. Trying harder doesn't change it.

The answer is on a stand. People "…set it on a stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house." A lit lamp gets put up where it can do its job. That's what Jesus says people do instead of putting it under a basket.
The word is deeds. Jesus says, "…let your light shine before men, that they may see your good deeds…" He's talking about what they do. Good deeds are what people get to see.
The answer is their Father in heaven. People see the good deeds and "…glorify your Father in heaven." The glory goes up to Him. That's where Jesus points this whole thing.
